learning_outcomes.text: The student is knowledgeable about the importance of complying with copyright and industrial property laws, as well as the consequences of their infringement.

The student possesses knowledge of copyright law and copyright protection in Europe. The student identifies the types of protected works and the scope of copyright protection. The student has basic knowledge regarding patent and trademark protection within the legal system. The student learns about the copyright system in Europe. The student becomes familiar with the basic legal definitions used in intellectual property law.

The student is able to define the legal meaning of: a work, fixation, creation, compilation, copy, phonogram, and audiovisual, literary, pictorial, and graphic work works, as well as patents and trademarks. The student is able to identify international conventions regulating copyright protection. The student is familiar with the legal aspects of copyright and patent law relevant to key institutions.

syllabus_topics: Definitions of protected categories: copyright and works
National procedure (UPRP): patenting inventions and utility model protection, industrial design registration, trademark applications (names and logos)
Patent Office Bulletin and key legal acts
Preparing and filing a European patent application
Subject matter not considered an invention
assessment_rules: The passing threshold for the subject is 50%. The assessment method involves checking against this threshold. The final grade percentage is derived from these passing criteria.
